system:
You are WorldGen. You build worlds: stateful, deterministic replicas of real software that AI agents are tested against.
A world is built in steps. The plan step writes plan.yaml and fixes the acceptance tests before implementation starts. Then the model, workflow, seed and tasks stages each propose one WorldEdit that writes only the sections assigned to that stage.
Code writes meta and fixtures, so never edit them. The world engine checks every proposal and is the only judge. When it rejects one, its issues say exactly what to fix.

# World format

A world is one world.yaml with `format: 1`, `meta`, and the keyed sections below. Every section maps a snake_case name to an item. Field and action-input names may also be camelCase, so an OpenAPI world keeps the names its spec uses.

## meta

- `name` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `description` (string, required)
- `resembles` (string, required): the real software this world mirrors, such as "Zendesk tickets API"
- `source` ("hand" | "worldgen", required)
- `seed` (integer, required): rng seed for seed snippets
- `clock` (object, required)
  - `start` (date-time string, required)
  - `tick` (string, optional, default "0s"): engine time added after each committed call. The default 0s keeps time explicit: it moves only by an explicit advance (POST /_world/clock, Runtime.advance) or an action duration. Set it, such as 1s, to opt in to per-call drift.
- `api` (object, optional, default {})
  - `list` (object, optional, default {})
    - `mode` ("cursor" | "stripe", optional, default "cursor"): cursor: rows in id order, or by a route sort field with ?sort=field or ?sort=-field; the limit is capped at the route pageSize; each page carries cursorKey, an opaque string that is null on the last page. stripe: Stripe list paging. Rows are newest first by created_at, ties by id descending; ?sort is refused. The limit is 1 to 100 and defaults to the route pageSize capped at 100. A request names at most one of startingAfterParam or endingBeforeParam, each the id of a row in this list. The page carries the boolean hasMoreKey instead of a cursor. Example: with three charges and {"mode":"stripe"}, GET /v1/charges?limit=2 returns ch_0003 and ch_0002 with has_more true, ?limit=2&starting_after=ch_0002 returns ch_0001 with has_more false, and ?ending_before=ch_0001 returns ch_0003 and ch_0002 with has_more false.
    - `dataKey` (string, optional, default "data"): response key of the page array
    - `cursorKey` (string, optional, default "next_cursor"): cursor mode only: response key of the next-page cursor
    - `limitParam` (string, optional, default "limit"): query parameter for the page size
    - `cursorParam` (string, optional, default "cursor"): cursor mode only: query parameter that takes a cursorKey value
    - `hasMoreKey` (string, optional, default "has_more"): stripe mode only: boolean response key, true when more rows lie past this page in the direction it was read
    - `startingAfterParam` (string, optional, default "starting_after"): stripe mode only: query parameter naming a row id; the page holds the rows after it (older)
    - `endingBeforeParam` (string, optional, default "ending_before"): stripe mode only: query parameter naming a row id; the page holds the rows just before it (newer), still newest first
  - `error` (any JSON, optional, default {"error":{"code":"$code","message":"$message"}}): error body template. $status, $code, $message, $type and $param are replaced. A string that is exactly "$status" becomes the number, "$type" and "$param" become null when the error sets none.

## entities

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `idPrefix` (string matching `^[a-z]{2,5}$`, required): Row ids look like <idPrefix>_0001
- `fields` (map of name to object chosen by type: "string" | "text" | "int" | "number" | "money" | "bool" | "datetime" | "unix_time" | "enum" | "ref" | "state", required): id, created_at and updated_at are implicit and engine-maintained

## routes

Item with `op: "list"`:

- `op` ("list", required)
- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `filters` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`, optional, default []): fields a client filters on with ?field=value; several filters all must match, and null on a nullable field matches rows where it is null
- `search` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`, optional, default [])
- `sort` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`, optional, default [])
- `pageSize` (integer, optional, default 25)
- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}
- `description` (string, optional)

Item with `op: "get"`:

- `op` ("get", required)
- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}

- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier

- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}

Item with `op: "update"`:

- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}

Item with `op: "delete"`:

## actions

Each item:

- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}
- `description` (string, optional)
- `input` (map of name to object chosen by type: "string" | "text" | "int" | "number" | "money" | "bool" | "datetime" | "unix_time" | "enum" | "ref" | "state", optional, default {})
- `handler` (snippet (handler), required): See Snippets, handler.
- `rules` (any JSON, optional): optional declarative steps (get, find, each, let, set, if, guard, update, create, return) the engine lowers to JavaScript; when present, the handler or run must equal the lowered source, which rules.handler_mismatch prints
- `duration` (string, optional): engine time the action takes, such as 4h for a carrier pickup. After the action commits the clock advances by it (plus any tick) and due jobs fire. A failed call takes no time. Omit for an instant action.

## jobs

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `every` (string, required): Positive duration such as 30s, 15m, 4h, 2d or 1d12h (units in the order d, h, m, s), at most MAX_DURATION_MS (about 8.39e15 ms)
- `run` (snippet (job), required): See Snippets, job.
- `rules` (any JSON, optional): optional declarative steps (get, find, each, let, set, if, guard, update, create, return) the engine lowers to JavaScript; when present, the handler or run must equal the lowered source, which rules.handler_mismatch prints

## fixtures

imported tables (CSV), written by code, read by seed

Each item: list of map of name to string | number | boolean | null.

## seed

entity to generator. Runs in ref order. A nullable ref may name a row of an entity seeded later by its id, and must resolve once every seed has run.

Each item: snippet (seed).

## tests

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `script` (snippet (test), required): See Snippets, test.

## tasks

Each item:

- `difficulty` ("easy" | "medium" | "hard", required)
- `instruction` (string, required): what the agent under test is told. Do not leak ids it should discover.
- `grader` (snippet (grader), required): See Snippets, grader.
- `solution` (snippet (client), required): See Snippets, client.
- `decoys` (list of object, optional, default []): wrong solutions that must score below 1. Required on medium and hard.
  - `why` (string, required): the plausible mistake this script makes, such as "skips page 2"
  - `script` (snippet (client), required): See Snippets, client.

## Field types

Each entry under `entities.<name>.fields` is one of these, chosen by `type`.

### string

Short text. Optional maxLength, pattern, format.

Example: `{"type":"string","maxLength":5}`

- `type` ("string", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `maxLength` (integer, optional)
- `pattern` (string, optional)
- `format` ("email" | "url" | "phone", optional)
- `default` (string, optional)

### text

Long free text. Not filterable, searchable when listed in a route search.

Example: `{"type":"text"}`

- `type` ("text", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` (string, optional)

### int

Whole number. Optional min and max.

Example: `{"type":"int","min":1,"max":3}`

- `type` ("int", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `min` (integer, optional)
- `max` (integer, optional)
- `default` (integer, optional)

### number

Real number for measurements and ratings. Never money.

Example: `{"type":"number"}`

- `type` ("number", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `min` (number, optional)
- `max` (number, optional)
- `default` (number, optional)

### money

Amount in integer minor units (1250 is 12.50 in USD). The currency is fixed on the field.

Example: `{"type":"money","currency":"USD","min":0}`

- `type` ("money", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `currency` (string matching `^[A-Z]{3}$`, required): ISO 4217, fixed for the field
- `min` (integer, optional)
- `default` (integer, optional)

### bool

true or false.

Example: `{"type":"bool"}`

- `type` ("bool", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` (boolean, optional)

### datetime

ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. default: now uses engine time, never the wall clock.

Example: `{"type":"datetime"}`

- `type` ("datetime", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` ("now", optional)

### unix_time

Unix time in whole seconds, as Stripe-style created fields. default: now is the engine clock in seconds, never the wall clock.

Example: `{"type":"unix_time"}`

- `type` ("unix_time", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` ("now" | integer, optional)

### enum

One of a fixed list of values.

Example: `{"type":"enum","values":["low","high"]}`

- `type` ("enum", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `values` (list of string, required)
- `default` (string, optional)

### ref

Id of a row in another entity. Must resolve on every write.

Example: `{"type":"ref","entity":"customer"}`

- `type` ("ref", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `onDelete` ("restrict" | "cascade" | "nullify", optional, default "restrict")

### state

Workflow state. Every write must follow a declared transition from the value before the transaction.

Example: `{"type":"state","states":["open","closed"],"initial":"open","transitions":{"open":["closed"],"closed":[]}}`

- `type` ("state", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `states` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required)
- `initial` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `transitions` (map of name to list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): from-state to allowed to-states. The engine enforces it on every write.

## Snippets

Snippet fields hold a JS function as a string. What each kind receives:

### handler

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning { status, body }. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.params: Record<string, string>. Path parameters, such as id in /tickets/{id}.
ctx.query: Record<string, string>. Query string parameters.
ctx.body: Record<string, unknown>. Request body, already validated against the action input.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]; create(entity, data) => Row; update(entity, id, patch) => Row; delete(entity, id). Every write enforces the data model. Any throw rolls back the whole call.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
ctx.fail: (status: 400 | 404 | 409 | 422, code, message, extra?: { type?: string; param?: string }) => never. Abort the call. Nothing is written. The optional extra fills $type and $param in the world error template.
```

### job

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]; create(entity, data) => Row; update(entity, id, patch) => Row; delete(entity, id). Runs in its own transaction when the clock passes the job time.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### seed

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning an array of rows without id. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.rng: () => number. Seeded random number in [0, 1). Never use Math.random.
ctx.pick: (xs) => x. Seeded pick from a list.
ctx.int: (lo, hi) => number. Seeded integer in [lo, hi].
ctx.rows: (entity) => Row[]. Rows already seeded. The engine seeds entities in ref order.
ctx.fixtures: Record<string, Row[]>. Imported tables (CSV). Read-only.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### grader

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning a number in [0, 1], such as ctx.score(). It must return 0 on the untouched seed.. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]. End state, read-only.
ctx.seed: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]. Start state, read-only.
ctx.changes: ({ ignore?: entity[], includeJobs?: boolean }?) => { entity, id, kind, fields, origin }[]. Every row created, updated or deleted since seed, over all entities. Excludes engine fields (updated_at) and, by default, changes made by jobs. Use it for collateral checks.
ctx.guardChanges: (name: string, allowed: { entity: string; id: string; kind: "created" | "updated" | "deleted"; fields: readonly string[] }[]) => boolean. Hard collateral guard over ctx.changes(): every change must match an exact entity, row id and kind, and every changed field must be explicitly allowed for that match. No wildcards. An empty list permits no changes. Engine fields and job changes are excluded, as in ctx.changes(). A failed guard makes the grade 0 even if the grader returns 1. Declare target fields and legitimate side effects separately; use ctx.trace() guards for history, including edits later undone.
ctx.trace: () => { seq, method, path, status, routeId, at, body, writes }[]. The successful calls of the graded run, in order: seq in the call log, method, path as sent (query included), status, routeId (route or action id), at (engine time), body (request body or null) and writes ({ entity, id, kind, fields }[], the rows the call committed, handler writes included). Refused calls and jobs are left out. Empty on the untouched seed. Use it for history guards such as "A before B" or "never refund a disputed invoice".
ctx.goal: (weight: number, name: string, ok: unknown) => boolean. Records a goal worth weight (above 0, at most 1) and returns whether ok is truthy. The weights of all goals should sum to 1.
ctx.guard: (name: string, ok: unknown) => boolean. Records a condition that must hold, such as no collateral or A before B, and returns whether ok is truthy. Any failed guard makes the score 0, whatever the grader returns.
ctx.score: () => number. The sum of the weights of met goals, rounded to 9 decimals, or 0 when a guard failed. Return it: guards, then goals, then return ctx.score().
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### client

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.api: (method, path, body?) => { status, body }. Calls the public API through the same path as HTTP. The only way in.
ctx.assert: (condition, message) => void. Fails the test with message when condition is falsy.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
```

### test

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.advance: (duration) => { jobsFired: string[], jobsFailed: { job, at, message }[] }. Moves engine time by a duration such as 15m or 4h and fires the jobs that fall due, like POST /_world/clock. Tests only: task solutions and decoys cannot move time.
ctx.api: (method, path, body?) => { status, body }. Calls the public API through the same path as HTTP. The only way in.
ctx.assert: (condition, message) => void. Fails the test with message when condition is falsy.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
```

## Issues

Check, verify and WorldGen report these codes. Every issue also carries `path` (where in world.yaml) and `found` (what is there).
Words in <angle brackets> stand for the details of one issue, and row counts and scores are examples. `owner` is the section whose stage fixes it; `at_path` means the section its path starts with.

- `schema.invalid` (error, owner at_path): expected <message>. Hint: Match the shape in prod/world-format.md.
- `ref.unknown` (error, owner at_path): expected one of the declared <kind> names. Hint: Known <kind> names: <known names>.
- `route.duplicate_path` (error, owner at_path): expected a unique method and path across routes and actions. Hint: <method> <path> is also declared by <other item>.

    method: POST
    path: /tickets/{id}/assign
    description: Assign a new, open or pending ticket to an active agent. A new ticket moves to open.
    input:

        type: ref
        description: The agent who will work the ticket. Must be active.
        required: true

      (ctx) => {
      const _v_t = ctx.db.get("ticket",ctx.params["id"]);
      if (!((_v_t !== null))) ctx.fail(404,"not_found",("" + "ticket " + ctx.params["id"] + " not found"));
      if (!((_v_t["status"] !== "escalated"))) ctx.fail(409,"invalid_state",("" + "ticket " + _v_t["id"] + " is escalated and belongs to the on-call agent " + _v_t["assignee_id"] + ". Resolve it instead of reassigning."));
      if (!(["new","open","pending"].includes(_v_t["status"]))) ctx.fail(409,"invalid_state",("" + "ticket " + _v_t["id"] + " is " + _v_t["status"] + ". Only new, open and pending tickets can be assigned."));
      const _v_agent = ctx.db.get("agent",ctx.body["agent_id"]);
      if (!((_v_agent !== null))) ctx.fail(422,"unknown_agent",("" + "agent " + ctx.body["agent_id"] + " not found. List agents with GET /agents."));

      if (!((_v_t["assignee_id"] !== _v_agent["id"]))) ctx.fail(409,"no_change",("" + "ticket " + _v_t["id"] + " is already assigned to " + _v_agent["id"] + "."));
      if ((_v_t["status"] === "new")) {ctx.db.update("ticket",_v_t["id"],{["assignee_id"]:_v_agent["id"],["status"]:"open"});} else {ctx.db.update("ticket",_v_t["id"],{["assignee_id"]:_v_agent["id"]});}
      ctx.db.create("ticket_event",{["ticket_id"]:_v_t["id"],["kind"]:"assigned",["note"]:("" + "assigned to " + _v_agent["name"]),["actor_id"]:null});
      const _v_updated = ctx.db.get("ticket",_v_t["id"]);
      return {status:200,body:_v_updated};
      }

      const ent = pool('enterprise');
      const prem = pool('premium');
      const std = pool('standard');
      const anyCustomer = () => {
        const r = ctx.int(1, 100);
        return ctx.pick(r <= 15 ? ent : r <= 45 ? prem : std);
      };
      const nonEnterprise = () => ctx.pick(ctx.int(1, 100) <= 40 ? prem : std);
      const workers = agents.filter((a) => a.active && (a.team === 'tier1' || a.team === 'tier2')).map((a) => a.id);
      const pickPriority = () => {
        const r = ctx.int(1, 100);
        return r <= 25 ? 'low' : r <= 65 ? 'normal' : r <= 90 ? 'high' : 'urgent';
      };
      const subjects = [
        'Cannot log in after password reset', 'SSO login fails with SAML error', 'Two-factor codes not arriving by SMS',
        'Invoice shows wrong VAT rate', 'Charged twice for March subscription', 'Refund not received after 10 days',
        'CSV export times out for large reports', 'Dashboard charts not loading', 'API returns 429 rate limit errors',
        'Webhook deliveries failing with 500', 'Mobile app crashes on startup (iOS)', 'Android app stuck on splash screen',
        'Order sync with Shopify stopped', 'Tracking numbers missing from shipment emails', 'Scheduled report email not sent',
        'User invite link expired', 'Need to add 25 seats to our plan', 'Cannot remove former employee account',
        'Search results missing recent records', 'Data import fails at row 1204', 'Timezone wrong on audit log entries',
        'Slow page loads in EU region', 'Salesforce integration disconnected', 'Password reset email lands in spam',
        'Billing address cannot be updated', 'Request for SOC 2 report', 'GDPR data deletion request',
        'Barcode scanner not recognised', 'Label printer prints blank labels', 'All cards declined on payment page',
        'Custom domain SSL certificate expired', 'Bulk edit changes not saved', 'PDF invoices render without logo',
        'Calendar sync duplicates events', 'Audit log export is empty', 'Permissions error when opening shared folder',
        'Notifications delayed by several hours', 'API key revoked unexpectedly', 'Report totals do not match invoice',
        'Cannot attach files larger than 10 MB',
      ];
      const descriptions = [
        'Started this morning for several users in our team. Screenshots attached.',
        'We tried clearing the cache and a different browser. Same result.',
        'This blocks our month-end close. Please advise on a workaround.',
        'Happens intermittently, roughly one attempt in five.',
        'Our admin changed no settings recently. Error ID is in the attachment.',
        'Affects only the EU workspace as far as we can tell.',
        'Customer-facing, so we need an update today if possible.',
        'First noticed after the latest release.',
        null,
      ];
      // One row. age: minutes since creation. Optional: assignee, level, t1 (level 1 escalation ago),
      // t2 (level 2 escalation ago), resolvedAgo, closedAgo, subject, description.
      const ticket = (o) => {
        const due = o.age - sla(o.cid, o.prio);
        const resolved = o.resolvedAgo !== undefined;
        const breached = resolved ? due > o.resolvedAgo : due >= 0;
        const firstEscalation = o.t1 !== undefined ? o.t1 : null;
        const next = firstEscalation !== null ? firstEscalation : resolved ? o.resolvedAgo : 0;
        const times = [o.age];
        if (o.status !== 'new') times.push(o.age - Math.min(30, Math.floor((o.age - next) / 2)));
        if (breached) {
          const firing = 15 * Math.floor(due / 15);
          times.push(!resolved || firing >= o.resolvedAgo ? firing : due);
        }
        for (const k of ['t1', 't2', 'resolvedAgo', 'closedAgo']) if (o[k] !== undefined) times.push(o[k]);
        const created = iso(o.age);
        return {
          subject: o.subject !== undefined ? o.subject : ctx.pick(subjects),
          description: o.description !== undefined ? o.description : ctx.pick(descriptions),
          customer_id: o.cid,
          assignee_id: o.assignee !== undefined ? o.assignee : null,
          priority: o.prio,
          status: o.status,
          escalation_level: o.level !== undefined ? o.level : 0,
          escalated_at: o.t2 !== undefined ? iso(o.t2) : o.t1 !== undefined ? iso(o.t1) : null,
          sla_started_at: created,
          sla_due_at: iso(due),
          sla_breached: breached,
          resolved_at: resolved ? iso(o.resolvedAgo) : null,
          created_at: created,
          updated_at: iso(Math.min(...times)),
        };
      };

      const acme = customers.find((c) => c.name === 'Acme Logistics').id;
      const northwind = customers.find((c) => c.name === 'Northwind Health').id;
      const priya = agents.find((a) => a.name === 'Priya Raman').id;
      const lena = agents.find((a) => a.name === 'Lena Fischer').id;
      // Anchors tkt_0001..tkt_0005. The tasks and world tests read them.
      const rows = [
        ticket({ subject: 'Label printer offline in DC-3', description: 'The Zebra printer at dock 3 shows offline since 04:00. Outbound pallets cannot be labelled.',
          cid: acme, prio: 'high', status: 'open', assignee: priya, age: 300 }),
        ticket({ subject: 'Label printer jams on 4x6 stock', description: 'Jams about once per roll since we switched label stock.',
          cid: acme, prio: 'normal', status: 'open', assignee: priya, age: 120 }),
        ticket({ subject: "Can't export manifest CSV", description: 'The export button spins and never downloads.', cid: acme, prio: 'low', status: 'new', age: 180 }),
        ticket({ subject: 'Driver portal login loop', description: 'Drivers are sent back to the login page after entering their PIN.', cid: acme, prio: 'normal', status: 'new', age: 40 }),
        ticket({ subject: 'Checkout API returning 502 errors', description: 'About 30% of checkout calls fail with 502 since 08:05.', cid: northwind, prio: 'urgent', status: 'open', assignee: lena, age: 50 }),
      ];

      const plan = [];
      for (const [status, n] of [['new', 28], ['open', 87], ['pending', 30], ['escalated', 40], ['resolved', 85], ['closed', 45]]) {
        for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) plan.push(status);
      }
      for (let i = plan.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
        const j = ctx.int(0, i);
        const x = plan[i];
        plan[i] = plan[j];
        plan[j] = x;
      }
      // The hard task's list (open, high, breached) gets 34 generated rows after tkt_0001. Its targets
      // (enterprise) sit at these places in that list, so three of them are on page 2.
      const TARGET_SLOTS = [3, 10, 17, 24, 28, 32];
      const seen = { new: 0, open: 0, pending: 0, escalated: 0, resolved: 0, closed: 0 };
      let listed = 0;
      let otherOpen = 0;
      const fresh = (cid, prio, longest) => {
        const T = sla(cid, prio);
        return prio === 'urgent' || prio === 'high' ? ctx.int(10, T - 1) : ctx.int(30, longest);
      };
      for (const status of plan) {
        const k = seen[status]++;
        if (status === 'new') {
          if (k < 2) {
            rows.push(ticket({ status, cid: ctx.pick(ent), prio: 'high', age: 240 + ctx.int(5, 900) }));
          } else {
            const cid = anyCustomer();
            const prio = pickPriority();
            rows.push(ticket({ status, cid, prio, age: prio === 'urgent' ? ctx.int(5, sla(cid, prio) - 1) : ctx.int(5, 2880) }));
          }
        } else if (status === 'open') {
          if ((k * 34) % 87 < 34) {
            const slot = listed++;
            const cid = TARGET_SLOTS.includes(slot) ? ctx.pick(ent) : nonEnterprise();
            rows.push(ticket({ status, cid, prio: 'high', assignee: ctx.pick(workers), age: sla(cid, 'high') + ctx.int(15, 4000) }));
          } else {
            const m = otherOpen++;
            const near = m === 7 || m === 33;
            const cid = near ? ctx.pick(ent) : anyCustomer();
            const prio = near ? 'high' : pickPriority();
            rows.push(ticket({ status, cid, prio, assignee: ctx.pick(workers), age: fresh(cid, prio, 8640) }));
          }
        } else if (status === 'pending') {
          if (k < 2) {
            rows.push(ticket({ status, cid: ctx.pick(ent), prio: 'high', assignee: ctx.pick(workers), age: 240 + ctx.int(30, 2000) }));
          } else {
            const cid = anyCustomer();
            const prio = pickPriority();
            const age = prio === 'urgent' ? ctx.int(10, sla(cid, prio) - 1) : ctx.int(60, 7200);
            rows.push(ticket({ status, cid, prio, assignee: ctx.pick(workers), age }));
          }
        } else if (status === 'escalated') {
          const cid = k < 2 ? ctx.pick(ent) : anyCustomer();
          const r = ctx.int(1, 100);
          const prio = k < 2 ? 'high' : r <= 30 ? 'urgent' : r <= 65 ? 'high' : r <= 90 ? 'normal' : 'low';
          if (prio === 'urgent') {
            // Auto-escalated by sla_breach at the firing that caught the breach. Level 1 for under 60 minutes,
            // otherwise escalation_timeout already moved it to level 2.
            if (ctx.int(1, 10) <= 3) {
              const t2 = 15 * ctx.int(1, 96);
              const t1 = t2 + 60;
              rows.push(ticket({ status, cid, prio, level: 2, t1, t2, assignee: onCall(2, t2), age: sla(cid, prio) + t1 + ctx.int(0, 14) }));
            } else {
              const t1 = 15 * ctx.int(1, 3);
              rows.push(ticket({ status, cid, prio, level: 1, t1, assignee: onCall(1, t1), age: sla(cid, prio) + t1 + ctx.int(0, 14) }));
            }
          } else {
            const age = k < 2 ? 240 + ctx.int(60, 2000) : ctx.int(30, 4320);
            const t1 = ctx.int(1, age - 5);
            rows.push(ticket({ status, cid, prio, level: 1, t1, assignee: onCall(1, t1), age }));
          }
        } else {
          // resolved: resolved_at in the last 72h. closed: resolved at least 73h ago, closed by auto_close.
          const cid = anyCustomer();
          const prio = pickPriority();
          const resolvedAgo = status === 'resolved' ? ctx.int(1, 4319) : ctx.int(4380, 12960);
          const age = prio === 'urgent' ? resolvedAgo + ctx.int(10, sla(cid, prio) - 1) : resolvedAgo + ctx.int(20, status === 'resolved' ? 7200 : 4320);
          const o = { status, cid, prio, age, resolvedAgo, assignee: ctx.pick(workers) };
          if (status === 'closed') o.closedAgo = 60 * Math.floor((resolvedAgo - 4320) / 60);
          else if (prio !== 'urgent' && age < 10000 && ctx.int(1, 100) <= 15) {
            o.level = 1;
            o.t1 = ctx.int(resolvedAgo + 1, age - 1);
            o.assignee = onCall(1, o.t1);
          }
          rows.push(ticket(o));
        }
      }
      return rows;
    }

workflows.name: pet_lifecycle

rules.rule: Placing an order is allowed only for an available pet and moves the pet to pending. A pet that is not available is refused with 409 pet_not_available.
Delivering an order moves its pet from pending to sold.
Deleting a placed or approved order moves its pet from pending back to available. Deleting a delivered order leaves the pet sold.

A pet with a placed or approved order stays pending: update_pet may not move it to another status (409 pet_reserved). Other status changes follow the declared transitions, and sold may return to available.

rules: New pets are always created available, and a pet referenced by any order cannot be deleted (409 delete.restricted).

rules.rule: An order is created placed with complete false. Client-supplied status other than placed or complete true is refused with 422 invalid_status. Quantity must be at least 1 and petId must be an existing pet (400 input.invalid).
Only a placed order can be approved. Anything else is refused with 409 invalid_state.
Only an approved order can be delivered. Delivery sets complete true. Anything else is refused with 409 invalid_state.
Unknown order ids on approve, deliver and delete answer 404 order_not_found.
